description: We are Martian Phoenix, a multidisciplinary team passionate about space exploration, science, and emerging technologies. Our interests span planetary science, AI, Machine Learning, software development, 3D visualization, and immersive technologies.
summary:
Terra Twin is a free, no-login web tool that helps teams find places on Earth resembling Mars’s Jezero Crater for training and equipment testing. Built for NASA Space Apps, it focuses on the deserts and dry riverbeds of the Middle East and North Africa, a region that has seen little screening for Mars analogs.

Using NASA climate, elevation and imagery data alongside global elevation tiles, Terra Twin scores each 1° × 1° cell for terrain similarity, dryness and suitability for rover driving. Users can adjust the weights, explore the map, compare a 60 km stretch of terrain side by side with Jezero in 3D, and drive a virtual rover across it. A WebXR mode is available but still awaits headset testing.

Mission teams, researchers and educators can use Terra Twin to shortlist sites and see why each one scores well. In a six-site check, terrain similarity alone did not clearly distinguish known analogs from other sites, so the tool shows all three scores separately. Its roughly 500 m resolution supports regional screening, while assessing rover-scale terrain requires finer data.
details:
Terra Twin is a free, no-login web tool that screens 1,650 land cells across the Middle East and North Africa for potential Mars practice sites. We compare each cell’s slope, roughness and elevation relief with Jezero Crater, then score dryness and rover slope suitability separately. Users can adjust the weights to see which locations rise or fall and why.

The same terrain can be explored at three scales. Users can select a cell on a regional map, compare a 60 km section side by side with Jezero in 3D, and drive a virtual rover across it in an arcade game. Our goal is to help researchers shortlist locations for fieldwork and give educators a hands-on way to teach planetary terrain.

We kept the scores separate because a flat, dry site may be worth investigating for rover trials even if it looks little like Jezero. In our six-site test, terrain similarity alone failed to distinguish four known analogs from two controls. We published that result. The coarse elevation data, lack of mineral data and provisional rover slope limit restrict the tool to regional screening.

We built Terra Twin on team laptops using Python for analysis and JavaScript with React, Leaflet and three.js for the website. We used NASA POWER climate data, MOLA elevation data, Mars Trek and GIBS imagery, and AWS Terrain Tiles. Docker and Nginx serve the site.
